name: DragonSwordNativeWorldRadarPostRender

blockers: Confirm the applicable Unreal Engine and UEPseudo authorization, redistribution, and GPL-compatibility terms for the generated interface used by the binary.
Record and review the exact e_sqlcipher.dll source revisions, patches, build recipe, toolchain, and reproducible source-to-binary chain.

Review redistribution rights and attribution/provenance for the PAK-derived catalogs, MnMRadar-derived coordinate tables, and ActorPositionData-derived Area Quest height-band profiles before publishing them.
public_release_clearance.boundary: Technical build, package, deployment, gameplay, and performance acceptance do not clear third-party publication rights or source-provenance obligations.

compatibility_contract.unsupported_policy: A structurally complete ExperimentalNested loader/proxy/settings/Mods layout is accepted without a fixed DLL-hash allowlist. Missing UE4SS bootstraps the embedded integrity-verified ExperimentalNested runtime. Root, dual, malformed, and incomplete layouts require confirmed complete-backup conversion.

game_executable.compatibility_policy: Require a bounded executable AMD64 PE32+ image at the exact game path; do not use an exact game SHA-256 allowlist.
game_executable.observed_sha256_usage: Transaction identity and install-record provenance only

release_acceptance.boundary: Historical 2.2.0 source, build, package, installer, and local-deployment evidence remains bound to DLL 6AEFDACC1A44EF6F387456CB31FE1A6828259EF7ACDEE1D1FE13BAE10BDFA4D5 and compiled source A98660932CC5DA1BC3E2B9D262DBFC13E0FED3935A6174B5C92E8622BBA2A1EC; it is not 2.2.1 evidence. Exact-artifact 2.2.1 source validation, build, package, Setup 20/20, Manual 2/2, payload equivalence, layout, clean-target, and three-archive byte-identical re-extraction passed for DLL 5F3414B44783E00F1DA3389301A05AD6953D5CEFDDB8B5C6DEF5F98E899B9B92 and compiled source 21B02B27F85D777E89AAD22CDEEB7B051BEDB2F13F6A05F126797D65DB204951. Developer-local deployment is tracked separately and is not package acceptance evidence. Gameplay, native-icon stability, click-target alignment, F6 visual behavior, controller behavior, localization, exit, and performance remain NOT_VALIDATED. Public publication remains BLOCKED independently.

source_archive_scope.excluded: SDK, RE-UE4SS, UEPseudo, FetchContent checkouts, Rust crates, build directories, and third-party toolchains
source_archive_scope.boundary: The source archive must not be represented as complete source for every dependency used to build or bundled with the binary.

renderer: Native UMG only. Version 2.2.1 is a fixes-only world-map ownership correction and adds no marker, menu, localization, height, catalog, capacity, style, or save feature. Compact radar and F6 behavior retain the 2.2.0 contracts. Expanded map 100 retains the fixed 4,096-entry eligible snapshot, two event-built 3072-by-3072 atlases, style revision 50, and the existing cached-Slate, DPI, zoom, independent-X/Y, player-anchor, and aspect-ratio projection chain. The game-native map-icon Canvas is now a read-only geometry witness: the Mod never inserts, removes, sizes, orders, prepasses, or hit-tests a child there. The two atlas hosts are independent hit-test-invisible viewport widgets added through AddToViewport and transformed from accepted native-Canvas geometry into viewport-local coordinates. Same-layer pan, zoom, DPI, and layout observations update only host transforms; they do not rerasterize, rebuild, reparent, or reproject marker data. Before the first valid transform, or after exact layer identity changes, transient unavailable geometry keeps the Mod hosts hidden for the existing bounded retry sequence. After a valid same-layer transform, a transient Canvas replacement or geometry-read gap retains the last verified placement and gated visibility. Only invalid Mod-owned payload, ABI, or guarded runtime state hard-faults and detaches. Production main.dll compiles and connects no PostRender/Present canary, external diagnostic mapping, executable, bridge, or Lua renderer.

native_provider.treasure_interaction_policy: The DsAnimationProp.NetMultiExecuteInteractProp pre-hook treats its context as the exact treasure Actor and accepts the event only when the reflected Actor parameter equals the freshly resolved local Pawn. The receiver's reported ObjectID is validated against exact class and 3D position first; if unavailable, an activation/epoch-matched weak observation or bounded unique-class 3D match may supply the save ID. DsAnimationProp.SetDeathProcess remains an exact-receiver fallback. These paths run only on real events and add no timer, poll, UObject enumeration, SQL work, dynamic queue, or frame work.

encounter_death_hook.registration: optional; missing, non-native, or failed registration reports a bounded disabled state and cannot fail required radar readiness
encounter_death_hook.acceptance: exact already-observed weak receiver, exact immutable catalog class, DsMonsterCharacter, current activation and epoch, current availability, visible_seen, and current player-to-Actor distance no greater than 100 metres
encounter_death_hook.callback_work: set one bit in a fixed 49-bit atomic mask only; retain no UObject and perform no scan, SQL query, dynamic queue, recurring timer, continuous poll, cooldown mutation, or renderer mutation
encounter_death_hook.consumer: ordinary consumption runs in the existing 250 ms control service only when enabled, non-transitioning, non-suppressed context and player position are valid; it does not recheck the accepted event's time window, applies the 120-minute cooldown/state, and clears each successfully applied or deduplicated bit independently; an apply exception retains that bit without erasing unrelated or newly published bits
encounter_death_hook.authoritative_boundary_policy: F7, disable, travel, and activity-suppression boundaries may settle pending cooldown and eligibility numerically without renderer mutation before reset; only safe live-GameThread finalization and the TitleMap owner boundary may hard-clear the 49-bit mask; true process teardown closes ingress and returns, and UObjectArray shutdown does not clear it
encounter_death_hook.steady_work_delta: none; the repair reuses the existing control service and adds no poll, timer, scan, SQL query, dynamic queue, renderer schedule, or steady work
encounter_death_hook.runtime_acceptance: Historical R4, 2.0.0, 2.1.0, and exact-byte 2.2.0 evidence remains historical; exact-artifact 2.2.1 native-icon stability, click-target alignment, controller-menu, localized F6, height guidance, world-map glyph styling, and regression acceptance remain NOT_VALIDATED

native_provider.discovery_policy: Treasure state is interaction/lifecycle driven and never schedules class catch-up enumeration. Boss and Assault use one weak slot per immutable encounter catalog index, populated by the UObject creation listener. The existing 250 ms discovery service walks those 49 slots round-robin, resolves the current exact-class Actor position before applying the 100-metre player-to-actor bound, and performs at most eight Actor-position queries per control tick. A live in-range Actor may refresh the last trusted numeric position; a later far pooled relocation may trigger range eviction but cannot overwrite that trusted fallback position. A non-Destroyed EndPlay cannot directly prove defeat. An already observed RemovedFromWorld clears the ended weak UObject and may continue only through the ordinary nearby ten-second numeric disappearance gate. Menu/activity suppression, travel, invalid position, unavailable encounter, stale or duplicate cooldown, duplicate identity, or leaving the last trusted actor position reject that gate. There is no FindAllOf, static catalog-distance prefilter, dynamic encounter queue, death-state poll, or 16 ms encounter work.
native_provider.encounter_confirmation_policy: Completion accepts either the optional DsFieldCharacter.NetMulticastNotifyDeath receiver event or the schema-validated NetMulticastSetDeathProcess receiver event only at DENM_ProcessState::End. Both routes still require exact observed weak identity, exact catalog class, DsMonsterCharacter, current activation/epoch, current availability, visible_seen, and current player distance within 100 metres. Each callback publishes only one fixed catalog bit; ordinary consumption waits for valid context and never rechecks an already accepted event's time window. The dev65 disappearance fallback remains unchanged: at least four present samples spanning one real second, followed by at least forty consecutive missing samples spanning ten real seconds while the player remains within 100 metres of the last trusted in-range position and every lifecycle, availability, and visibility gate remains valid. That fallback and strict exact-class Destroyed EndPlay recheck current time/cooldown at their final write. A visible already-observed RemovedFromWorld edge may start, but never complete, the missing window. A live actor return clears the missing sequence.
native_provider.encounter_edge_policy: An exact death event passes current availability before setting one bit in the fixed 49-bit atomic handoff. The existing 250 ms control service clears each successfully applied or deduplicated bit independently; an apply exception retains its bit. F7, disable, travel, and activity-suppression boundaries may numerically settle pending bits without renderer mutation before reset. Only safe live-GameThread finalization and the TitleMap owner boundary may hard-clear the mask; true process teardown closes ingress and returns, and UObjectArray shutdown does not clear it. The bounded 49-entry cooldown map survives F8/F7 and one-shot save timestamps merge by maximum. The same control service rate-limits one scalar earliest-expiry comparison to 1 Hz. Only a reached cooldown edge or displayed world-hour change recomputes one fixed 49-bit visibility mask. An availability change or observed live-actor return dirties compact selection for one normal rebind and retires an attached atlas only when effective world-map visibility changed; the 16 ms motion path performs no 49-entry work.
native_provider.departure_policy: Treasure candidates retain their existing ten-second type-specific departure grace. Boss and Assault candidates are evicted without completion when the player leaves the 100-metre last-trusted-in-range-position bound. An already observed RemovedFromWorld clears the ended weak UObject and retains numeric evidence only for the ordinary nearby ten-second disappearance gate; unobserved removal, menu/activity suppression, and travel reject and clear the sequence.
native_provider.observed_removed_from_world_policy: RemovedFromWorld is never direct defeat evidence. A visible encounter that was already observed may retain numeric ID, last trusted in-range position, visibility history, and fixed confirmation counters after its weak UObject is cleared. The exact EndPlay edge may start the missing window when a short Assault did not survive long enough for ordinary one-second arming, but it must still pass forty missing 250 ms samples spanning ten seconds while the player remains within 100 metres and every lifecycle, availability, and cooldown gate remains valid. Opening the cursor-owning map cannot erase this ended numeric evidence; travel/activity suppression still clears it, and a returned Actor cancels the sequence.
native_provider.open_world_return_policy: The confirmed open-world return edge starts one bounded compact attachment/rebind cycle from current availability and fresh weak candidates; it does not reuse a suppressed-world encounter disappearance sequence or schedule steady retry work.
native_provider.retained_uobject_policy: weak object index and serial only; no Pawn, Controller, Canvas, World, actor, task actor, task class, task container, or reflected array-element pointer crosses a callback
native_provider.travel_policy: InitGameState pre-transition first drains already published exact area-task completion bits into activation-local numeric completion and prerequisite evidence and settles accepted encounter-death bits into numeric cooldown/eligibility without renderer mutation. It then clears task-class mapping/atomic state, detaches renderers, resets weak runtime identities, increments the epoch, and enters the fail-closed transition cooldown. Exact completion witnesses retain only fixed numeric catalog indices, their original ten-second deadlines, 750 ms probe schedules, and counters; F8/F7 clears them. The drains and witness state access and retain no UObject.

engine_tick_recovery.fault_boundary: The engine-tick entrypoint is SEH guarded. A native fault immediately disables publication and records one pending recovery decision for the next valid engine tick.
engine_tick_recovery.budget_scope: process lifetime; F7, F8, travel, and successful recovery never replenish it
engine_tick_recovery.eligibility: the interrupted radar must have been enabled and the next tick must supply a current Engine
engine_tick_recovery.cleanup: spend the single budget before cleanup, disable the radar, publish disabled state, detach the world-map renderer explicitly, reset world-map runtime state, and start only one fresh bounded activation
engine_tick_recovery.failure_policy: a cleanup or activation fault, an inactive interrupted radar, a missing Engine, or an exhausted budget stops recovery fail closed; no second automatic attempt is possible
engine_tick_recovery.steady_state: no watchdog, timer, polling loop, retry queue, or recurring recovery work

save_behavior.sql_policy: One full below-normal native worker reconciliation is requested for every F7 activation after the first valid player sample. A valid single-owner result records an exact per-ID COMPLETE_CNT baseline, treating an absent requested ID as zero only in that valid result; invalid or ambiguous ownership leaves the baseline unknown. An inconclusive exact witness queues no confirmation SQL for an unknown baseline. With a known baseline, one event-driven exact-ID confirmation may run immediately through the same single worker, with at most two later retries spaced 15 seconds apart; only strict count growth confirms completion. Every confirmation skips tb_treasure_box and reads only tb_actor_respawn plus exact requested rows from tb_dynamic_quest_complete; it is not periodic and tb_dynamic_quest_group is never queried.
save_behavior.retry_policy: The initial full request retries submission only while a stale prior activation request is still being collected. For each exact witnessed area-quest ID with a known F7 COMPLETE_CNT baseline, completion confirmation is due immediately and may retry twice at 15-second intervals, for three attempts total. Equal, lower, ambiguous, mismatched, unavailable, and failed results change no state. After three non-confirming attempts the same task generation is locked against repeated-event replenishment; only a new F7 or current NONE or END followed by later ACCEPTABLE or PROGRESS unlocks a new generation. Fixed deadlines and counters never create a recurring SQL schedule.
save_behavior.callback_limits: SQLite C callbacks catch every C++ exception and fail closed above 4096 treasure rows or 65536 encounter/dynamic-completion rows
save_behavior.f8_policy: invalidate pending work and publish no late result
save_behavior.native_delta_policy: Immediately remove an exact treasure or linked mini-game reward at the game-owned interaction boundary. NetMultiExecuteInteractProp requires either the fresh local Pawn or, for a mount-only treasure within eight metres, that Pawn's exact callback-local Rider UObject with a non-null same-World relationship. The exact receiver resolves through ObjectID/class/3D, with observed weak identity or bounded unique-class 3D fallback; SetDeathProcess and positive-observation plus 10-second disappearance confirmation remain bounded fallbacks. Every other rejected non-Pawn interaction is never immediate completion. Only an exact treasure receiver within eight metres of the fresh local player may queue its fixed catalog bit for a positive-only exact-category save check after 15 seconds and one final check 285 seconds later. Each below-normal request carries at most 64 IDs, skips encounter and dynamic-quest SQL, holds no UObject, and performs no poll. Treasure and linked mini-game application dirties compact selection only on a real eligibility 1-to-0 transition. A changed map-100 entry rebuilds in the current session only when the exact retained layer is visibly open; a hidden attached layer is retired and deferred until the next SetWorldMapImage edge. Duplicate IDs return before generated-catalog matching and cause no additional dirty state, atlas invalidation, or rebuild. An exact accepted Boss/Assault NetMulticastNotifyDeath receiver or schema-validated NetMulticastSetDeathProcess End receiver publishes one fixed catalog bit; the existing 250 ms control service consumes it, applies the 120-minute cooldown, and invalidates rendering. No hook callback performs SQL, enumeration, continuous polling, or atlas work. Ordinary disappearance remains the strict dev65 fallback and can hide an available target only after four present samples over at least one second followed by forty consecutive missing samples over at least ten seconds while the player remains within 100 metres of the last trusted in-range actor position and no menu, suppression, or travel boundary is active. An already observed RemovedFromWorld clears the ended weak UObject and may continue only through that same ordinary gate; the EndPlay event itself never completes the encounter. Departure rejects completion, and a returned actor resets missing evidence and causes normal compact rebinding. Strict exact-class Destroyed EndPlay remains a secondary immediate route through the same current-availability and bounded actor/catalog/player evidence. The bounded encounter cooldown map survives F8/F7, and one-shot save timestamps merge by maximum so an older snapshot cannot revive a newer native defeat. An exact dynamic catalog quest event may arm a ten-second exact-ID witness without prior PROGRESS but never completes the task by itself. If exact END remains unverified at expiry, that fixed catalog bit may request an immediate coalesced positive-only exact-ID completion confirmation through the single below-normal worker and at most two retries spaced 15 seconds apart. Every confirmation skips treasure SQL; negative, ambiguous, mismatched, unavailable, or failed results change no state, and the three-attempt bound is not periodic SQL. The compact snapshot refreshes on its next existing update; expanded-map work rebuilds immediately only for an exact visibly open retained layer and otherwise waits for the next SetWorldMapImage edge, so closed-map gameplay pays no atlas-build cost. Process-lifetime deltas override a stale save snapshot. Asynchronous dynamic-task publication merges only positive completion IDs, so an older F7 result cannot erase newer runtime completion evidence.
save_behavior.area_quest_save_confirmation_policy: The full F7 single-owner query records an exact COMPLETE_CNT baseline for each requested area-task ID; only there may an absent ID become baseline zero. Invalid or ambiguous ownership leaves the baseline unknown, and an unknown ID cannot queue event-driven confirmation SQL. With a known baseline, positive-only means strictly greater COMPLETE_CNT for that exact ID, never merely a positive historical row. Three non-confirming attempts lock the current task generation against repeated event rearming. Only a new F7 or a current NONE or END sample followed by later ACCEPTABLE or PROGRESS starts a new unlocked generation.
save_behavior.encounter_death_handoff_policy: Accepted event bits are consumed only in valid ordinary context or at an authoritative F7/disable/travel/activity-suppression boundary. Ordinary consumption does not recheck the accepted event's time window. Successful bits clear individually, apply exceptions retain their bits, and lifecycle drains perform no renderer mutation. Only safe live-GameThread finalization and the TitleMap owner boundary may hard-clear the mask; true process teardown closes ingress and returns, and UObjectArray shutdown does not clear it. No new scheduling or steady work is introduced.
save_behavior.delayed_result_atlas_policy: If the one-shot F7 result arrives after an expanded atlas was attached, applying the numeric result rebuilds immediately only when the exact retained layer is visibly open. A hidden or detached layer is retired and deferred until the next exact SetWorldMapImage edge.

runtime_boundary.native_owner: all collection, selection, projection, and UMG rendering remain inside main.dll
runtime_boundary.main_menu_owner_boundary: The exact World /Game/Title/TitleMap/DS_Title.DS_Title identity disables the radar, detaches both renderers, clears weak candidates and mutable save-owned runtime state, and latches activation off. Loading another save remains disabled; F7 is rejected until a fully loaded open-world identity exists and then must be pressed explicitly. The edge reuses existing transition/world identity signals and adds no new poll, enumeration, or SQL.

native_event_log.config_policy: read exactly once during native construction; the current form accepts at most 2048 bytes with one diagnostics section and exactly one debug_logging=true or debug_logging=false key, while allowing comments, blank lines, and surrounding horizontal whitespace. The exact legacy single line event_log_enabled=true or event_log_enabled=false with an optional final line ending remains accepted. Missing, unreadable, oversized, duplicate-section, duplicate-key, unknown, non-canonical Boolean, lone-carriage-return, or malformed input fails closed to disabled; no hot polling is implemented
native_event_log.stream_policy: when explicitly enabled, one process-lifetime persistent output stream is guarded by one mutex; logger failure closes and atomically disables only logging without disabling radar runtime
native_event_log.disabled_policy: the default disabled path creates no log directory, opens or rotates no file, and returns through one atomic check before formatting, mutex acquisition, or file work; existing historical logs are left untouched
native_event_log.retention_policy: one bounded current file plus one replaced previous file; startup and size rollover never accumulate additional generations
native_event_log.critical_flush_policy: START, F7_ACTIVATED, F8_DISABLED, RADAR_ACTIVITY_SUPPRESSION, and every event containing FAILED, FAULT, DISABLED, or REJECTED flush immediately. COMPACT_POOL_STATE and WORLD_MAP_STATE use the bounded ordinary batch.
native_event_log.privacy: local only and excluded from packages, but may contain player/target coordinates, world/class names, catalog/task IDs, and lifecycle timing; redact before public sharing
native_event_log.runtime_acceptance: pending for exact-artifact 2.2.1; the installed gameplay-test copy may be explicitly enabled through the live config while the packaged release default remains disabled

visibility_hub.implementation: transient localized native UMG responsive framed card with weak widget identities, live viewport/DPI fit scaling with a minimum margin, centered placement, and role-scaled text; sections separate Mod Status, Language, marker visibility, three compact height controls, display modes, and Bug Report so all controls remain visible at supported aspect ratios
visibility_hub.text_vertical_centering: Source lifecycle centering covers initial open, language changes, status changes, and popup visibility changes. Each eligible TextBlock retains its authored line-box geometry; unavailable, faulting, non-finite, non-positive, or oversized desired-size evidence preserves that authored geometry. Reflow is edge-only and changes no per-frame path, radar or world-map geometry, or checkbox/button hit region. Live F6 visual acceptance remains NOT_VALIDATED.
visibility_hub.compact_only_categories: bird-eggs; independent F6 RADAR toggle with unavailable MAP cell
visibility_hub.area_quest_display_mode: AVAILABLE preserves prerequisite-proven visibility; ALL displays catalog tasks not excluded by saved or exact runtime completion, while a current active repeatable cycle remains visible
visibility_hub.assault_display_mode: AVAILABLE preserves save readiness, authored Assault time windows, defeat state, and the future 120-minute cooldown; ALL is a presentation-only static view of all 40 Assault records and ignores those live filters without mutating completion or cooldown authority; switching back to AVAILABLE restores the live filters; Boss and area-quest selection are unchanged
visibility_hub.height_arrow_controls: Treasure, Area Quest, and Mole default on for a clean configuration; valid existing choices are preserved. Treasure controls the unchanged nearest retained six-piece left-side arrow. The persisted Mole key controls the one nearest-mini-game below-icon triangle shared by Fly, Mole, and Wave. Area Quest controls height state for every visible task marker. No switch hides its marker or changes gameplay state.
visibility_hub.language_control: The centered selector face and popup expose only the eleven explicit game UI languages; AUTO and Use Game Language are not displayed. A legacy persisted AUTO value is migration input only: the next actual F6 opening or F7 activation reads DGameUserSettings.LanguageText, falls back to the Kismet language provider and English, persists the matching explicit preference, and performs no later automatic language sampling. On the first real F6 opening, one bounded loaded-Font enumeration caches the exact DsCompositFont_CommonSystem, DsCompositFont_TCSystem, DsCompositFont_JPSystem, and DsCompositFont_THSystem objects. Each language selects its matching cached game font; the complete live FSlateFontInfo is copied and only FontObject is replaced, preserving size, spacing, outline, and material state. Missing optional font evidence falls back without rejecting F6, and no recurring font scan or file work is added.
visibility_hub.status_control: F6 may open while Radar is Off, On, or Faulted. The status action is Enable, Disable, or Retry. Enable uses the same loaded-playable-world guard as F7. Status presentation changes only on an edge, and commands are one-shot.
visibility_hub.apply_policy: one packed game-thread transaction for both masks, both display modes, the three-bit height-arrow mask, and language preference plus one atomic config-file replacement only on a real selection change; compact selection updates immediately, language-only changes update the open panel, and only world-visible category or display-mode changes coalesce one expanded-map rebuild on X or F6 close
visibility_hub.close_policy: top-right X or second F6; no Apply or Cancel controls
visibility_hub.cursor_policy: Game-and-UI mode before cursor-visible write; conditional open-only repair after an observed hide
visibility_hub.closed_state: one owner boolean branch; no UObject access, reflection, allocation, polling, or file I/O
visibility_hub.travel_policy: guarded pre-transition RemoveFromParent and input restoration through the panel host owning controller; weak handles clear fail closed
visibility_hub.config: The current config/visibility.ini accepts at most 4096 bytes and requires complete readable [radar], [map], [modes], [height_arrows], and [interface] sections. Named visibility and height values use true or false, both modes use available or all, and language uses one canonical preference ID. The prior exact three-section format and strict legacy schema 1-4 packed-mask documents remain accepted and migrate to all three height controls on and AUTO language. The file is loaded once at startup, never hot-polled, atomically rewritten only on a real F6 change, and preserved by deployment. Duplicate, mixed-format, unknown, incomplete, malformed, or inconsistent-line-ending input falls back to safe defaults.
visibility_hub.fault_recovery: F6 is the only recovery trigger for a prior runtime-only Faulted Hub. Recovery requires a current Controller, a zero ABI-failure mask, and a guarded detach that introduces no new fault before returning to Ready. A same-detach fault or any ABI fault remains terminal for that attempt. Hub recovery neither arms nor consumes automatic engine-tick recovery.

historical_canary_artifacts.status: source-only, uncompiled, and disconnected from the production owner
historical_canary_artifacts.purpose: preserve audited development history and static retirement gates only

compact_umg_renderer.attachment: One validated current-controller player-icon Blueprint host provides the realized WidgetTree and cleared root Canvas. Its one moving child owns 80 preallocated four-piece slots for treasure, Boss, Sudden Missions, mini-games, Area Quests, and runtime-only bird eggs plus one unchanged Treasure six-piece height group and one retained nearest-mini-game triangle group; Area Quest height reuses each marker's existing pieces. The fixed clock remains a root sibling. No second player-tree or encounter root is created. F8, travel, confirmed non-open-world activity, the exact TitleMap save-owner boundary, and shutdown clean the single host through weak identities.
compact_umg_renderer.diagnostic_witness: No copied player-arrow witness is compiled or attached. Fixed channels follow the nearest Treasure and nearest retained Fly/Mole/Wave marker. Treasure retains its selected type color and unchanged full six-piece pointer to the left of the selected chest. Every visible Area Quest first selects the uniquely nearest source band using the marker's authored Z, then evaluates that selected band in the existing bounded marker pass: the original black frame shows three white dots inside the inclusive +/-500 margin, points up below the band, and points down above it. Missing profiles or an exact nearest-band tie remain neutral with no dots or direction; no separate task arrow exists. Geometry changes only on a discrete state edge. The nearest-mini-game shaftless triangle is centered directly below the selected icon, uses that marker's actual kind palette, points up for target Z more than 500 vertical units above the comparable player Z, points down for target Z more than 500 below, and hides in the inclusive +/-500 band. Runtime motion otherwise changes only fixed numeric transforms and state-edge geometry.
compact_umg_renderer.viewport_reflow_policy: The existing one-hertz minimap-scale service also reads viewport size and DPI. An unchanged sample performs no layout mutation; a real geometry edge updates the retained host top-left render scale, viewport position, and one layout prepass so compact markers and the fixed clock move together across window/fullscreen changes.
compact_umg_renderer.selection_policy: Up to 80 markers within the live game minimap radius. Selection is bounded across unopened treasure, 9 Boss, 40 Sudden Missions, 33 Fly, 40 Mole, 10 Wave, 147 Area Quest records, and at most 16 current runtime bird eggs. Area Quests render when current state is ACCEPTABLE or PROGRESS, or when the one-shot completion snapshot confirms the catalog task is uncompleted and its Main/Group prerequisite proof is positive. A confirmed exact mapped completion hides immediately and remains latched through stale or still-active samples until a current NONE or END boundary followed by a later current ACCEPTABLE or PROGRESS sample proves repeatable reactivation. Unknown conditions and unresolved weighted group selections stay hidden. Exactly one nearest Treasure may use the unchanged category-colored six-piece full height pointer to the left of its chest, every retained visible Area Quest may use its independent aligned/up/down/neutral state from the marker-Z-selected height band, and one nearest retained Fly/Mole/Wave marker may use the below-icon, actual-kind-colored up/down triangle only when its exact NPC_Start height is trusted and outside the inclusive +/-500 band. The three user switches gate only this height guidance.
compact_umg_renderer.steady_state: Exactly one SetRenderTranslation ProcessEvent moves the single compact root with one numeric transform per accepted 16 ms position sample. No marker child is touched and viewport layout is not invalidated. The fixed clock is a root sibling and never receives motion transforms. Area quests are scanned at one ID per game frame only after F7, completed travel, a coalesced quest-state callback burst, or a displayed game-hour edge. Dev54 exact completion publishes one fixed atomic catalog bit and applies immediate numeric hide on the next game tick, then reuses generic transactional refreshes for settled-state proof: current NONE or END arms reactivation and only a later current ACCEPTABLE or PROGRESS sample may restore a repeatable task. Completed quest rows are read only inside the existing one-shot F7 save snapshot, whose asynchronous result merges positive completion IDs without clearing newer runtime evidence.
compact_umg_renderer.cleanup: RemoveFromParent on F8, travel, confirmed non-open-world activity, exact TitleMap save-owner boundary, and shutdown. Ordinary cursor-owning menu suppression uses Collapsed without destroying the single host. The open-world activity return edge can begin one fresh renderer activation while the radar remains enabled; after TitleMap, activation stays latched off until an explicit F7 in a fully loaded open world. An exact new DLayerMiniMap from the UObject-create weak mailbox can rearm and supply one bounded attachment instead of uncollapsing an old-world host.
compact_umg_renderer.retry_policy: at most three attempts per F7 activation or travel epoch; a distinct exact DLayerMiniMap create identity may rearm one budget while enabled and outside transition or confirmed non-open-world suppression, even when the old renderer still reports attached or menu-suppressed; duplicate identity delivery and ordinary soft failures do not replenish it; transition end validates the deferred weak candidate against the exact new GameMode world; no sleep or steady loop
compact_umg_renderer.fault_recovery: Only an explicit activation boundary or confirmed open-world activity return may recover a prior runtime-only Faulted renderer. The recovery first clears all weak runtime handles through guarded detach and returns to Ready only when the detach adds no fault and the ABI-failure mask is zero. Same-detach faults and ABI faults remain terminal; no idle retry is scheduled.

bird_egg_runtime.persistence: runtime-only; no immutable catalog or save state
bird_egg_runtime.presentation: compact-only with independent F6 RADAR category and no MAP category
bird_egg_runtime.candidate_storage: fixed 512-slot FWeakObjectPtr pool populated only by the UObject creation listener
bird_egg_runtime.active_presence_schedule: shared existing discovery edge; no independent timer
bird_egg_runtime.availability_source: exact Actor-owned DInteractableComponent exposed through InteractComponent
bird_egg_runtime.available_state: exact one-byte scoped-enum FEnumProperty reads through validated integer underlying properties, with InteractableValue=2 and InteractTypeValue=2
bird_egg_runtime.unknown_state_policy: retain the fixed weak candidate and retry on the existing bounded 250 ms service; never guess available and never retire from one unknown read
bird_egg_runtime.end_play_policy: exact Bird Egg EndPlay immediately retires the matching weak identity
bird_egg_runtime.retention: weak identity and copied numeric position only; no raw Actor retained

area_quest_state.height_policy: The 147 tasks contain 144 ActorPositionData-derived height profiles selected from MapGroupID 100 by exact numeric task-ID name boundary and at most 1000-unit planar distance. Candidate Z values are clustered into bands separated by gaps greater than 250 Unreal units; Move_Check-only trigger bands are excluded when a real task-actor band exists. A valid multi-band profile is collapsed to the uniquely nearest existing source band using the catalog marker's authored Z only as stage-selection evidence; an exact nearest-band tie fails closed. The selected source band then compares against playerZ minus 150 and uses an inclusive +/-500 alignment margin. The three no-source rows remain neutral, and marker Z never becomes a synthetic height target.

area_quest_state.task_class_mapping: After F7 or completed travel, a guarded reflection reads GameInstance.TaskActorClassContainer.DynamicQuestTaskList. Dynamic TaskUseType rows join CreateTaskClass full names through a single unambiguous UseQuestList ID to the validated area-quest catalog. Direct identity is enabled only with exactly 147 one-to-one catalog bindings and zero ambiguous classes or duplicate catalog coverage. Capture permits one post-stability attempt and only one delayed retry after failure; success or the second failure stops all work. Completed travel may start a fresh bounded capture; an already-active explicit F7 rearms only failed capture and preserves completion bits, revisions, and reactivation latches. Confirmed non-open-world activity suppression defers pending capture until open-world rendering resumes. Only copied strings and catalog indices are retained.
area_quest_state.triggerability_policy: F7 copies numeric Main/Group rows from the loaded DDynamicQuestDataTable through DGameSingleton.GameDBTableManager, then discards every UObject. NONE records render only when supported conditions are positively proven. Current MONSTER_ALIVE rows with value1=0 link only when exactly one Assault exists inside the bounded 150-metre task neighborhood and then reuse its cooldown and world-time availability; nonzero unknown semantics, zero candidates, and multiple candidates remain fail closed. Unknown condition kinds, unavailable tables, failed prerequisite queries, unlinked monsters, and unresolved weighted selections fail closed. Current ACCEPTABLE or PROGRESS is authoritative only when no completion latch is active or after the required current NONE-or-END boundary and later current active sample complete repeatable reactivation.
area_quest_state.world_map_source: eligible current runtime ACCEPTABLE or PROGRESS after completion-latch fencing, plus uncompleted catalog tasks whose loaded DynamicQuest Main/Group conditions are positively proven from NONE, ordinary QUEST_CLEAR state, saved DYNAMIC_QUEST_COMPLETE state, or the linked MONSTER_ALIVE Assault availability; unknown definitions and weighted-selection ambiguity stay hidden
area_quest_state.save_user_policy: accept only one positive USER_DBID; a mixed-user newest readable source terminates optional task augmentation instead of falling back to an older backup, and logs the selected identity or ambiguity
area_quest_state.completion_count_policy: COMPLETE_CNT greater than zero means previously completed for the initial expanded-map filter. A generic runtime scan may latch only PROGRESS-to-END. A schema-validated dynamic ETSendQuestEventTrigger for one exact 147-entry catalog ID arms that numeric witness without a prior PROGRESS requirement; this event proves identity but is never completion. Exact OnQuestBlueprintEndPlay and OnRenewQuestBlueprintEndPlay task Actors may also arm the same catalog index only through the complete unambiguous task-class map. Generic interaction is treasure-only. Each exact witness keeps one original ten-second deadline, a 750 ms exact-ID probe schedule, and one deduplicated index in a fixed 147-entry queue. All witnesses share a hard budget of one reflected exact-ID query per engine tick, and repeated events cannot extend a live deadline or duplicate its queue entry. Final END proves the exact witnessed task complete even when the preceding published state was NONE, FAIL, ACCEPTABLE, or PROGRESS; NONE alone is not completion and every unwitnessed END remains non-proof. An unresolved expiry queues that fixed catalog bit for one immediate positive-only exact-ID save confirmation and at most two retries spaced 15 seconds apart on the single below-normal worker. Negative, ambiguous, mismatched, unavailable, and failed results change no state; the three-attempt bound never becomes periodic SQL. On native ADETTaskBaseActor.OnRecvCompleteQuest, the current task actor class full name is mapped to one exact catalog index, published through a fixed atomic bit mask, and applied as immediate numeric completion on the next game tick. If InitGameState pre-transition arrives first, it drains already published bits into the same activation-local numeric completion and prerequisite evidence before clearing mapping and atomic state, without UObject access or retention. Fixed per-task revisions prevent a scan started before that event from reviving the task with stale ACCEPTABLE or PROGRESS. Later still-active current scans also preserve completion until a current scan first observes NONE or END; only a subsequent current scan may rearm a genuinely repeatable task on ACCEPTABLE or PROGRESS. FAIL does not arm reactivation. The asynchronous one-shot F7 snapshot and event-driven confirmations merge only positive completion IDs and cannot clear newer native completion evidence. A retained expanded atlas rebuilds immediately only when its exact layer is visibly open; otherwise it is retired and deferred to the next SetWorldMapImage session. F8 followed by F7 remains a fresh resynchronization.
area_quest_state.save_confirmation_baseline_policy: F7 establishes the exact per-ID COMPLETE_CNT baseline only from a valid single-owner query. A requested ID absent from that valid result has baseline zero; invalid or ambiguous ownership leaves it unknown. Unknown baseline queues no confirmation SQL. A confirmation applies only strict count growth above the known baseline. Three non-confirming immediate or 15-second attempts lock the same task generation; repeated events cannot replenish it. A new F7 unlocks directly, or current NONE or END followed by later ACCEPTABLE or PROGRESS proves and unlocks a new repeatable generation.
area_quest_state.schedule: One reflected query per game frame during an ordinary transactional refresh: 147 dynamic task states followed by deduplicated ordinary QUEST_CLEAR prerequisites. Refreshes are triggered by F7, completed travel, a one-second-coalesced quest teardown/task/native quest-event burst capped at two seconds, the first valid clock sample after F7, or one coalesced scan after a later displayed game-hour edge. Separately, an exact witnessed task may receive one exact-ID query every 750 ms inside its original ten-second window, with a global maximum of one witness query per engine tick and no duplicate or replenishing queue entry. The task-class identity table permits one post-stability attempt per F7/travel and one delayed retry only after an initial failure; success or the second failure stops all work. Exact mapped completion hides immediately and does not wait for the generic scan. Linked MONSTER_ALIVE visibility refreshes on Assault defeat, first valid clock state, and displayed hour edges. Completed-quest SQL remains confined to the existing single below-normal save worker: once in the full F7 reconciliation, or for an expired exact witness immediately and at most twice more at 15-second intervals. No independent idle query timer exists.
area_quest_state.failure_policy: Task-class mapping ignores classes used only outside the 147-entry catalog, but a class shared by a catalog ID and any other ID is ambiguous because its completion callback cannot distinguish them. Exactly 147 one-to-one catalog bindings are required. Missing schema, invalid bounds, ambiguous class IDs, duplicate or incomplete catalog coverage, and unmapped completion callbacks cannot hide a guessed task and fall back only to the generic transactional refresh. SEH-guarded runtime scan failures preserve the last complete snapshot when available. Optional completion SQL fails closed only for global task augmentation, and mixed-user identity ambiguity forbids older-backup fallback.
area_quest_state.fault_recovery: A scan fault preserves the last complete published snapshot when one exists, publishes nothing partial, fails closed on a first-activation fault, and schedules no automatic retry for the rest of that activation. Only an explicit F7 starts a new bounded activation and clears the scan-fault latch.

The Radar payload contains build metadata, immutable diagnostics-disabled and visibility defaults, exactly ten generated data catalogs, treasure overrides, e_sqlcipher.dll, release/provider/inference metadata, required licenses and notices, and the generated package manifest. Setup normalizes exactly one DragonSwordNativeWorldRadarPostRender : 1 entry, removes every valid DragonSwordWorldRadarObjectState entry instead of retaining a redundant disabled line, preserves unrelated bytes, and backs up and removes a recognized same-product legacy enabled.txt only as migration input. An active or malformed DragonSwordWorldRadar entry or exact DragonSwordWorldRadar/enabled.txt path in any approved Mods root causes a zero-mutation reject; exact disabled DragonSwordWorldRadar : 0 is preserved, and Setup never deletes or disables that external renderer. release_layout.deployment_policy: The unsigned elevated Setup selects the exact game executable path and validates a bounded executable AMD64 PE32+ image without a fixed game-hash allowlist. A structurally complete ExperimentalNested UE4SS layout is accepted by bounded x64 PE32+ DLL and directory checks without loader/proxy hash compatibility gates. Conversion retains its complete original-layout backup. Setup refuses a running game and never launches or terminates it. If validation against the active .db fails during FullActivation, runtime permits at most one current-EXE unique structural scan plus the same bounded key discovery; structural incompatibility fails closed, and compatibility is not promised for every future game version. validation_status: Version 2.2.1 is a fixes-only technical release candidate. It keeps every 2.2.0 marker, catalog, capacity, style, menu, localization, height, save, and installer feature unchanged while moving both world-map atlas hosts out of the game-native map-icon Canvas. The native Canvas is read only and used only as a geometry and player-icon witness; independent viewport-owned, hit-test-invisible hosts cannot participate in native desired-size, prepass, layout, Z-slot, or hit-test state. Same-layer valid observations update host transforms only and never rerasterize or rebuild marker data. Initial or different-layer transient gaps stay hidden inside the existing bounded retry sequence; same-layer gaps after a valid transform retain the last verified placement instead of faulting, detaching, or rebuilding. Exact-artifact 2.2.1 source validation, build, package, Setup 20/20, Manual 2/2, payload equivalence, layout, clean-target, and three-archive byte-identical re-extraction passed for DLL 5F3414B44783E00F1DA3389301A05AD6953D5CEFDDB8B5C6DEF5F98E899B9B92 and compiled source 21B02B27F85D777E89AAD22CDEEB7B051BEDB2F13F6A05F126797D65DB204951. Developer-local deployment is tracked separately and is not package acceptance evidence. Historical 2.2.0 build, package, installer, deployment, and hash evidence remains historical and is not relabelled. Gameplay, native-icon stability, click targets, pan/zoom, 4K 16:9, 21:9, 16:10, DPI, windowed modes, controller menus, dense Treasure, travel/reopen, exit, and performance remain NOT_VALIDATED. Public publication remains BLOCKED pending the recorded provenance and rights reviews.
performance_claim: Version 2.2.1 adds no timer, poll, enumeration, periodic SQL, dynamic queue, filesystem work, focus hook, controller-binding scan, language reflection, atlas allocation, atlas rerasterization, or marker-data rebuild. It replaces native-Canvas child ownership with two existing-capacity viewport hosts. The native Canvas remains read only; accepted same-parent geometry changes update only two viewport-host transforms. The 4,096-marker arrays and two 3072 BGRA atlases retain the 2.2.0 memory and event-only construction contract. These are static structural properties, not measured gameplay, visual, exit, memory, or frame-time acceptance.
